what_happened: Measured, compiled finding that redirects the gate: the depth-0 obligation's two counter regimes are kappa-SEGREGATED (clipIdx at 2<=B separates n+2<=c from c'<=n'+1), so the five landed forward-slack schemas discharge exactly one half of the collision space, and a compiled gap-0 collision at the periodicity fixpoint's own parameters (with a ladder path through each state) populates the other half. The dispatch's named crux (ForwardSlackWitnessed at a positive amount) therefore cannot lift the gate on its own.

The in-source docstring of forwardSlackWitnessed_iff_next_region_cnt_le (LadderCell.lean:1035) states 'the ORDINARY WINDOW REGIME c <= n + 1 is addressed by no landed inclusion, in either direction'. That is stale: cellAt_subset_of_window_raise (LadderWindow.lean:1690) addresses it in the UPWARD countdown direction under WindowIdleRunWitnessed and hroom : c + m*(P+1) <= n, carrying no pending-forever gap. The DOWNWARD direction in that regime is what is genuinely unaddressed.

Compiled the exact arithmetic deficit between ParamsOk and the landed step-fragment back-and-forth: Zrel_of_kappa_eq consumes 2*dFwd phi + 2 <= B while paramsOkK4 asks only 2*dFwd phi + 1 <= B, and the deficit bites at Bof itself (witness X p, Bof = 3, needs 4). A one-token (K4) repair plus the two owed threshold inequalities would land the depth-0 schema on the step fragment.

Neither lifting event was delivered. Refutation direction: all four compiled cell-separating families (thetaC, sigC b, mixC a k, dblC j) are diaF- or .stab-rooted, hence carry a stab letter in their subformula closure (compiled: diaF_not_stabFree, stab_not_stabFree), so none of them bears on the stab-free depth-0 schema; no refuting candidate at depth 0 exists in the tree. Positive direction: the open core is stab-free formulas WITH an unbounded U/S jump, which the step-fragment back-and-forth excludes by construction.

Compiled all five plan-pinned Lean Challenge signatures against the live tree at AUTHORING time via lean-challenge-snapshot.sh --dry-run --compile (exit 0). This mechanically confirmed the plan's load-bearing import-DAG finding: a single import of RaySummary.LadderStepFrag resolves CellLEZeroConstOfKappaEq, because LadderAgree sits in LadderStepFrag's closure via LadderStepFrag -> LadderRealize -> LadderChain -> LadderPump -> LadderAgree. The research report had left siting open; the plan can therefore commit to no new module, no new import, no mk_all run and no check-metalogic-cycles allowlist extension.

Measured at plan time that the settled route's (K4) repair (2*dFwd+1 <= B becoming 2*dFwd+2 <= B) does not merely break proofs but FALSIFIES three landed records: exists_kappa_collision_cellAt_ne_at_K4_clip (LadderRealize.lean:2135), exists_paramsOk_real_not_certAdmK (:2256) and the RESTRICTION CHECK example (KTypeSummaryAxiomTest.lean:3662). All three discharge ParamsOk via paramsOk_params at thetaC against a written clip of 3, at which the repaired forward conjunct demands 4. Resolved in-plan as one atomic-batch phase using the tree's own precedent for the FIRST (K4) repair (frozen paramsOkK4Pre/ParamsOkPre plus a not_paramsOkK4_two-style rejection record), so the collision is scheduled rather than discovered mid-proof. Also surfaced: LadderStepFrag.lean sits at 1695 lines against a declared longFile 1700, so any addition of 5+ lines invalidates the baseline.

Phase 1 go/no-go probe compiled green on the second attempt: the pure-syntax bound dBack+dFwd <= closure.card went through by the plan's named decomposition (two disjoint root-filters of the closure plus a local fsize monotonicity helper), and both threshold discharges fell out of paramsOkK3's two conjuncts by omega. Threshold feasibility verdict is GO; the step-fragment bridge route is live.

check-module-invariants.sh reports two FAILs after Phase 2, neither attributable-and-fixable here: (1) INV 3 stale generated inventory blocks (README.md, FormalSystem/Metalogic/README.md, RaySummary/README.md) caused by this task's new declarations -- owned by Phase 5 per the plan's gate-collision Condition 1 surface (a); (2) C16 roots baseline 5 NEW entries, all in BimodalLibTest.DiagnosticsTest and four BimodalTools modules this task never touches -- pre-existing out-of-scope baseline finding, Condition 4 forbids editing an out-of-scope file to force a repo-wide count to zero.

Phase 3's plan task said paramsOkPre_params should discharge the frozen conditions 'at the fixpoint's own four outputs' and that the two restated theorems' discharge becomes paramsOkPre_params with the written clip unchanged. Those two are incompatible as written: after the repair Bof thetaC = 4 while the written clip is 3, so a paramsOkPre_params stated at Bof cannot discharge either restatement. Resolved by stating paramsOkPre_params with the fourth argument written out as the PRE-REPAIR Bof body max (2*dBack+1) (max (2*dFwd+1) 2) -- the fixpoint's own fourth pre-repair output -- which is definitionally the written clip. Recorded as an altered deviation on the plan checklist item.

The plan's Risk row asserted no linter warning would arise because the promoted Zrel_of_kappa_eq body's 'show' lines are goal-statement annotations and so the sanctioned use. Falsified: linter.style.show flagged all three (they restate Zrel's clauses with the two LadderState projections reduced, which is a definitional change). Fixed by 'change' in all three places, the idiomatic non-linted replacement. Separately, Phase 3's rename to the longer _pre names pushed three LadderRealize docstring lines past the 100-character limit and the file past its 4800-line longFile baseline -- neither visible until a module rebuild in Phase 4, since CI builds with --wfail and a warning is a failure.

Phase 5's Scope Hypothesis named four probes as most likely to rot and said the script's labels are authoritative. All four did rot, but the repair shapes split two ways the plan did not anticipate: ladder-cell-obligation-refutation and ladder-chain-object-clip-refutation needed only numeric citation updates (Bof_chiD 9->10; Bof_chainC 7->8 plus the clip floor max (E chainC) 7 -> 8), while ladder-cell-agreement-refutation and ladder-step-fragment-gap-depth needed the frozen-copy re-pointing: their obstructions turn on collisions the repaired clip DISSOLVES, so RefutationTargetC, CountMoveTargetC, cellAt_const_of_kappa_eq_schema_refuted, no_fibre_equation_over_kappa, no_transferSys_links_collisions, mixC_refutes and sigC_refutes all had to move from ParamsOk to the library's new ParamsOkPre, via a probe-local BofPre. A measured side finding worth keeping: the repair buys back exactly the two smallest members of the mixC family (k=1,2) and nothing beyond, since the separated gap 3k+4 now exceeds the clip 2k+6 by k-2 rather than k-1.
git-commit-scoped.sh dropped 4 pathspec(s) from a commit: not contained in task #991's declared file_scope. See tags.dropped_paths for the full list.

All six phases closed in one dispatch with the deliverable landed sorryAx-free, and the heaviest phase (the atomic-batch (K4) repair) hit its Scope Hypothesis exactly: the falsification set was precisely the three declarations the plan enumerated at authoring time, with no fourth declaration going red on the unscoped build. The plan's decision to run threshold feasibility as a task-local go/no-go probe BEFORE touching (K4) paid for itself -- the pure-syntax bound compiled on the second attempt, so no library edit was ever made on an unmeasured hypothesis.

Self-inflicted and caught before returning: the Phase 6 plan-file annotation used a python slice whose end index came from s.index('## Lean Challenge Statements') searched from position 0, which matched Phase 4's own verification bullet citing that section by name rather than the section heading. The end index landed BEFORE the start index, so the slice was empty and the write duplicated ~115 lines (Phase 4's tail plus the whole of Phase 5) while leaving Phase 6 unedited. This is exactly the bounded-block-edit hazard: a multi-line splice reconstructing a file from its own string slices. Repaired by restoring the plan from the Phase 5 commit and re-applying the Phase 6 annotation with both anchors matched at LINE START and the end anchor asserted to come after the start.
